title: What does a Mermaid verifier check?
answer: Verify fails a diagram that Agentic Mermaid’s renderer cannot draw, warns about structural gaps such as an unlabelled branch out of a decision, and leaves what the labels mean unchecked

checks.question: The agent writes the second edge as A -->|no| D, and D appears nowhere else in the source. What does verify(flow) report?
checks.answer: ok: true and no warnings. Mermaid creates D where it is first used, as a rectangle labelled D, so the diagram draws and both exits of the decision carry labels. That the agent meant Database is the kind of thing verify leaves unchecked.

checks.question: Starting from the right diagram, the agent adds a second, unlabelled edge from Cached to Database: A --> C. Which edge does the warning name?
checks.answer: A->C#1. It is the second edge from A to C, so its count is 1, while the labelled edge to Database keeps A->C#0. One DECISION_BRANCH_UNLABELED warning, and ok stays true.

checks.question: Draw Cached as a rectangle, A[Cached], and leave both edges unlabelled. Does the verifier warn?
checks.answer: No: ok: true with no warnings. DECISION_BRANCH_UNLABELED is about the exits of a decision diamond, and a rectangle is not a decision, so there is nothing for it to flag.

checks.question: The agent deletes the whole line for the edge to Database and leaves the edge to Reply unlabelled: A{Cached} --> B[Reply]. How many warnings?
checks.answer: None: ok: true with no warnings. The warning is for a decision with two or more exits, and Cached now has one, so its one unlabelled exit is not flagged.

steps.title: This diagram sends a cache hit to the database
steps.line: Follow yes out of Cached: it reaches Database.
steps.caption: A cache hit follows yes to Database, while no leads straight to Reply. This reverses the intended cache behavior. Agentic Mermaid’s verify(flow) returns a report about the source. Will it accept this diagram?

steps.title: verify(flow) returns ok: true, with no warnings
steps.line: The dot follows the yes edge as drawn: from Cached to Database.
steps.caption: The source renders and both exits of the decision carry labels, so the report has no warnings, even though its yes path reaches Database. Its last line, taskCorrectness: not-checked, marks where the check stops. Verify fails a diagram that Agentic Mermaid’s renderer cannot draw, warns about structural gaps such as an unlabelled branch out of a decision, and leaves what the labels mean unchecked. The next two steps show the failure and the warning.

steps.title: Delete both labels, and the verifier warns twice
steps.line: Does a missing label turn ok false too?
steps.caption: DECISION_BRANCH_UNLABELED is the warning for a decision with two or more exits where one exit carries no label. Agentic Mermaid names an edge by its two ends and a count: A->C#0 is the first edge from A, Cached, to C, Database. The warnings identify the unlabelled paths to Reply and Database. The diagram still renders, so ok stays true. A missing label is structural information the verifier can detect; choosing the correct label needs task knowledge.

steps.title: Label them the right way round: the report does not change
steps.line: Same report beside both. Follow yes: Database above, Reply below.
steps.caption: Two set_label edits, each naming one edge, put yes on the path to Reply and no on the path to Database. The corrected diagram sits below the backwards one, and both reports say ok: true with no warnings. Following yes out of Cached tells them apart: a hit reaches Database above and Reply below. A check that a cache hit reaches Reply without querying Database would catch the backwards one; this page describes that missing check rather than implementing it.
